source_citation: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

morphology_source_reported.thorns: Long stout branched thorns on trunk; predominantly simple on branches, sometimes absent; 6–15(–40) cm long
morphology_source_reported.leaves: Once- or twice-pinnately compound; once-pinnate leaves with 10–14 leaflet pairs; twice-pinnate leaves with 2–8 pinna pairs
morphology_source_reported.flowers: Small; petals 4–6 mm long; lateral catkin-like racemes (genus-level)
morphology_source_reported.fruit: Flattened often twisted/contorted many-seeded pod, 10–40 cm long (key), 2–4 cm wide; sweet pulp around seeds
morphology_source_reported.diagnostic_characters: Numerous large branched thorns and long, twisted many-seeded pods vs. the shorter few-seeded pods of G. aquatica

habitat_source_reported: Stream bottoms and disturbed sandy slopes/open ground
